decisions.decision: POSIX-sh + awk marker splicer over Node templating
decisions.rationale: Repo is zero-Node at runtime; shell splicing is sufficient for 4 chrome partials

decisions.decision: Pre-commit hook as byte-identity gate (first git hook in repo)
decisions.rationale: Chrome drift impossible at commit time; dual-mode symlink install works in clones + worktrees

decisions.decision: Tailwind v4.2.2 binary pinned + auto-installed via make install-tailwind
decisions.rationale: Reproducible builds without requiring package manager

decisions.decision: 404 H1 mobile step-down (text-4xl → text-3xl) over clamp() fluid sizing
decisions.rationale: Stay on project's Tailwind step-function pattern; preserves nbsp binding trivially

decisions.decision: Python Pillow as ImageMagick fallback for one-shot raster pipeline
decisions.rationale: ImageMagick not installed; Pillow 11.3.0 already present and equivalent for PNG→multi-size ICO + 180×180 square padding

decisions.decision: Hand-download Tilda production PNG once, commit derivatives, forbid runtime hotlinking
decisions.rationale: Supply-chain hygiene; no runtime dependency on third-party CDN

decisions.decision: Tailwind whitespace-nowrap span for Russian numeric range binding
decisions.rationale: Auditable via grep, utility-first consistent, no stylesheet pollution

context_notes: v3.2 shipped cleanly in a single day: 2 phases, 6 plans, 11 requirements, zero plan revisions. Milestone archival required manual drift fixes because the `phase complete` CLI does not flip active-milestone checkboxes in bold format, and `milestone complete` CLI's one-liner auto-extract produced garbage for Phase 39 summaries. Retrospective in .planning/RETROSPECTIVE.md has full lessons learned. Session anti-patterns: Bash cwd drift into worktree during Wave 1 merge (recovered via cd back + ff-only); pre-authorized tooling deviations in executor prompts worked well for Pillow fallback; parallel worktrees for disjoint files + sequential worktree for shared files was the right wave structure.
